summary: The note describes the Infiniti J30, a rear-wheel-drive luxury sedan sold in Japan as the Nissan Leopard J Ferie. It went into production in April 1992 as a 1993 model and was positioned between the G20 and Q45 to compete with the Acura Legend. The note also covers its rounded, coupe-like styling and the design team behind it.
one_line: The Infiniti J30 was a rear-wheel-drive mid-size luxury sedan (Nissan Leopard J Ferie in Japan) launched in 1992 to compete with the Acura Legend.
key_facts: The Infiniti J30 was also known as the Nissan Leopard J Ferie in Japan.
The Infiniti J30 was a rear-wheel-drive luxury car.
The Infiniti J30 went into production on April 7, 1992 as a 1993 model.
The Infiniti J30 replaced the M30, which was a coupe.
The Infiniti J30 was launched in the United States after its competitor, the Lexus GS.
The Infiniti J30 was designed to slot between the smaller G20 and the larger Q45.
The Infiniti J30 was Infiniti's first mid-size sedan, intended to compete directly with the Acura Legend.
The Infiniti J30 had rounded styling that was uncharacteristic of the crowded executive car class.
Jerry Hirshberg, president of Nissan Design International (NDI), was chief designer for the Infiniti J30.
Doug Wilson was exterior designer for the Infiniti J30 in 1988-1989.
Design work on the Infiniti J30 was frozen in 1989.
A promotional video produced in 1994 referred to the Infiniti J30 as a "personal luxury sedan".
The promotional video's description was an attempt to define the Infiniti J30 as a four-door coupé.
The Infiniti J30 has the round looks of the Nissan Altima/Bluebird U13.
